messages:
alex: heads-up, saw a couple customer sessions hitting burst throttle on streaming. They get disconnected and can't resume. We need to decide accounting: count tokens on emit vs on ack when reconnect resumes.

maria: which org / key? any example ids?

alex: org 1302-prod; single key. Appears as short spikes: 4-6 concurrent streams for ~10s. Our per-key token/min bucket exhausted because we count tokens on emit and then on resume clients re-emit.

simon: we currently increment token counters on emit. So if a stream disconnects mid-token and client resumes, we'll double-charge unless we reconcile.

elaine: can we persist a resume cursor that indicates already-billed offsets? maybe mark tokens as tentative until final commit?

alex: proposed: two-phase accounting. Tentative charge on emit; final commit on stream close or explicit client ack. On client resume with a cursor, reclaim tentative tokens for that stream and only charge delta.

kyle: that implies per-stream state. How many tentative entries are we talking? could be millions — storage/ops cost could be high.

maria: we could keep a small TTL k-v entry per stream_id (redis) storing current billed_offset and tentative_count. TTL 30s after inactivity; GC cheap.

kyle: redis ops per token could blow up. Alternative: aggregate tentative counts per-key per-second and only store minimal per-stream cursor for reconciling. That reduces ops.

elaine: on the console side, we should show 'streaming burst usage' with a split line: tentative vs committed. That helps customers understand spiky billing.

alex: also add tracing metadata: span.tag 'quota_billing_phase' = tentative|committed when we emit tokens so traces show where throttles happen.

simon: SLA concern: enterprise/dedicated customers expect deterministic throttling. If we allow tentative bursts, they might exceed reserved capacity before committed reconciliation.

kyle: idea: different policies per deployment mode. For Dedicated and Private: strict immediate commit on emit (no tentative). For Hosted free-tier: two-phase tentative flow to reduce false positives.

maria: enforcement order: per-key first (to protect noisy keys), then per-org aggregate to catch multiple keys. We should keep both.

elaine: reconnect handshake UX: client sends resume cursor -> server returns 200 + {resume_accepted:true, billed_delta:N} or 409 + {reason:'cursor_mismatch'}. Clear error codes will reduce developer confusion in SDKs.

alex: agree. Implementation sketch:
 - API: POST /v1/streams/{id}/resume with {cursor}
 - Billing: tentative entries in redis keyed by stream_id
 - On resume: reconcile tentative entries, decrement tentative counters, commit only new tokens
 - Telemetry: metrics streaming.tentative_tokens and streaming.committed_tokens; tracing tag quota_billing_phase
 - Fallback: if redis unavailable, fall back to immediate commit and mark degraded (so customers can see).

simon: I can spike handshake + redis keying this week, include a small integration test.

kyle: I'll write a perf sim for stream cardinality and redis op rate and share results.

maria: I'll update console mockups to show tentative vs committed series and add a toggle to view resume events.

elaine: docs: add retry guidance and error code mapping for SDKs (resume acceptance vs conflict). Also recommend clients send small resumable checkpoints frequently.

quota-bot: deploy-checklist: create feature-flag streaming_resume_billing; add metrics streaming.tentative_tokens, streaming.committed_tokens; add trace tag quota_billing_phase.

alex: thanks all — follow-up sync Monday 09:00. I'll open a GH issue with the design sketch and link the perf/runbook.

maria: please add #product-review to the GH issue.

simon: will do.

alex: one more note — fallback behavior: if we decide to reclaim tentative tokens on resume, we must ensure reconciliation windows are large enough to cover client reconnects across common network blips (e.g., 60s). TTL choice matters.

kyle: noted, I'll include TTL sensitivity in perf tests.

elaine: also add a console alert when tentative tokens are reclaimed to show customers that their spikes were not billed finally. UX win. :thumbsup:

alex: ok wrapping. thanks everyone.
